# Coming from QB64pe

<!-- Written by tools/reference/reference.py render; do not edit. -->

Where QB64Rust does something other than QB64pe 4.7.0, the compiler it follows. Everywhere else a
program behaves as it does with QB64pe.
63 rows, from `docs/DIVERGENCES-QB64PE.md`, which also says why each was decided and what pins it.

| Id | Case | QB64pe 4.7.0 | QB64Rust |
|---|---|---|---|
| D-001 | LONG (and INTEGER, computed in 32 bits) overflow in `+ - *` | Default: wraps (`2147483647 + 1` = `-2147483648`, `x + 1 > x` false). `-O2`: undefined behaviour in the generated C++; `x + 1 > x` is **true** and `PRINT x + 1` prints ` 2147483648 ` (`verification\v11_wrap_o2.out.txt`, `.O2.out.txt`) | Always wraps in two's complement, in generated code (`-fwrapv`) and in constant folding |
| D-002 | `_INTEGER64` overflow in `+ - *` | Default: wraps (`x + 1 > x` false). `-O2`: `x + 1 > x` is **true**; the printed value still wraps (`verification\v12_wrap_int64.out.txt`, `.O2.out.txt`) | Always wraps, like D-001 |
| D-003 | `RETURN label` with no `GOSUB` pending | Raises error 3, then decrements the `GOSUB` counter anyway (`qb64pe.bas` 9948), so it wraps below zero and the next `GOSUB` crashes the program (exit code 139; `verification\v17_d_return_label_none.out.txt`) | Raises error 3 and leaves the counter at 0; a later `GOSUB` and `RETURN` work |
| D-004 | A store into a member of an array element whose index is out of range (`a(9).m = 5` for `DIM a(3) AS t`), with the program going on (`RESUME NEXT`, or `QB64PE_NOPROMPT=continue`). The same for an element of a member array, at every index on the way: `t.v(9) = 5`, `a(9).v(1) = 5`, `a(1).v(9) = 6`, `t.g(2, 9) = 8` (design D8 of `m2-defxxx-common-arrays`: the rule applied to more places, not a new decision). The same for an element of a `_DYNAMIC` member array through a parent index outside: `p(9).v(5) = 55` (widened 2026-10-14, user, `m3-typefields` design D9). The same for a number read by `READ` or `INPUT #` into such a place: `READ a(9).m`, `INPUT #1, a(1).v(9)` (`m3-typefields` task 4.2: the rule applied to more places, as the old compiler stores them as an assignment, `verification\v35_x62`). The same for a whole-array assignment to or from a member array of an element whose index is outside: `e(9).w() = s()` (widened 2026-10-15, Claude, `m3-whole-array-assign` design D3; confirmed by the user 2026-10-16). The same for `_ARRAYCOPY` to or from a member array of an element whose index is outside: `_ARRAYCOPY src() TO tt(3).b()`, `_ARRAYCOPY tt(0).b(1 TO 2) TO d(2)` (widened 2026-10-17, Claude, `m3-arraycopy` design D5; confirmed by the user the same day) | Raises error 9 and **writes the value into element 0** (`a(0).m` becomes 5; also for `STRING` members): `array_check` returns 0 after raising and member stores are not guarded (`verification\v18_b_member_store.out.txt`). For a member array, position 0 of the dimension whose index was outside: `t.v(9) = 5` sets `t.v(0)`, `a(9).v(1) = 5` sets `a(0).v(1)`, `a(1).v(9) = 6` sets `a(1).v(0)`, `t.g(2, 9) = 8` sets `t.g(2, 0)` (`verification\v24_h_member_store`, `v24_x313`). For a `_DYNAMIC` member, the member of element 0: `p(9).v(5) = 55` sets `p(0).v(5)` (`verification\v35_x58`). In a whole-array assignment the member array of element 0 stands in: a `STRING` member array is copied through it (`e(9).w() = s()` sets `e(0).w`), one of numbers is not (its `memmove` checks for a pending error; `verification\v36_x48`). `_ARRAYCOPY` copies through the member array of element 0, numbers and strings alike, as destination and as source (`verification\v41_j`) | Raises error 9 and stores nothing (a whole-array assignment and `_ARRAYCOPY` copy nothing, of any kind; the bounds of `_ARRAYCOPY` are still evaluated). A number is still evaluated before the indexes and a string after them, as measured (`v24_x316`), and the first error still wins (`a(9).m = ASC("")` reports 5). The same when an index raises with no error pending before it (`a(ASC("")).m = 6`: the old compiler writes `a(0).m`, `verification\v18_b_index_raises`), as an element store does. An index that raises while the value's error is pending cannot be told apart (the first error wins) and stores as the old compiler does |

| D-008 | A label and `CONST` on one line (`lbl1: CONST k = 4`) | Compile error ("NULL string; nothing to evaluate", or "Unexpected element '='", depending on the label's length; the prepass strips the label wrongly, `verification\v05_label_const`, `v05b_label_const_short`) | Compiles: the label, then the `CONST` |
| D-009 | A `_BIT * n` scalar with n > 32 | Its 8-byte C type gets 4 bytes, so a store overwrites 4 bytes of the `_BIT` scalar (of any width) allocated just before it; other variables are not hit (`verification\v04_accidental`, `v21_b_bit_overlap`) | Each variable has its own storage |
| D-010 | Printing an infinite SINGLE or DOUBLE (`PRINT 1 / z!`) | ` INF           ` (SINGLE) and ` INF              D     ` (DOUBLE): padding and a stray exponent letter (`verification\v02_errors`) | Printed without the padding and the stray `D`; the exact text is set when it is implemented, from what `STR$` gives |
| D-011 | A comma in `PRINT` to the console (`$CONSOLE`) | Windows: pads with spaces until the console window's cursor column is a multiple of 10, asked through a new `CONOUT$` handle each time (never closed); with stdout redirected the cursor never moves and the program writes spaces forever (`study\10` §2.2). Linux and macOS: one space (read, not run) | Same zones (10 on Windows, one space elsewhere: user, "do exactly as QB64pe"), but the runtime counts the console column itself: no hang when redirected, no handle leak. Output may differ only where something other than the program moved the console cursor |
| D-012 | Exit code after an unhandled runtime error (with `QB64PE_NOPROMPT=y`, or "continue? no"), and after a critical error (300 to 315, a failed `_ASSERT`, out of memory, libqb's other fatal ends) | 0 (`verification\v02c_no_handler`; every recording of `verification\` that ends in `Runtime error`) | 1, on every platform, console or window (the path is libqb's, shared by both; only console programs are tested); traced. A program that goes on after the error (`QB64PE_NOPROMPT=continue`, "yes") keeps the code its end gives. Built by the edits `tools\libqb\edits\d012-error-exit-code*.edit` of the copy of libqb (offered upstream, `UPSTREAM.md`) |

| D-015 | The message for a `$EXEICON` whose file is not there; the same for a `$EMBED` whose file is not there or is a folder (widened 2026-10-17, `m3-network-embed` design D3: the rule applied to one more metacommand, not a new decision) | "File '<folder>\name.ico' not found" with the folder it looked in for a name with `./`, and only the last part of the name for any other (`verification\v29_e04`, `e02`); for `$EMBED` "File '<folder>\name' not found" likewise (`v44_x07`, `x27`) | "the file `./name.ico` of `$EXEICON` is not found", "the file `./name` of `$EMBED` is not found": the name as the program writes it |

| D-017 | `$DEBUG` | Includes the IDE's debugger (vWatch: `vwatch.bi`, `vwatch.bm`), calls it on every line and links the sockets part; outside the IDE (no `QB64DEBUGPORT`) the first call sets it to return at once ever after, so the program prints what it prints without `$DEBUG` (`verification\v33_d01`–`d11`). vWatch's names are taken: a SUB named `vwatch_stoptimers` is "Name already in use" (`v33_x49`) | Writes no debugger code: `_DEBUG_` and `_SOCKETS_` are set as the old compiler sets them, the sockets part is linked as the old compiler links it (narrowed 2026-10-17, `m3-network-embed` design D7: `_SOCKETS_` compiles the network helper of the file included after the last line), and `-w` gives its warning "$DEBUG features only work from the IDE". **A program built here cannot be debugged from the QB64pe IDE**, and vWatch's names are free |

| D-021 | A dynamic member array, or a whole array of a type with one, used where it is not allocated: `_MEM(x.v())` after `ERASE x.v`; `GET #f, , p()` into an array `p` that `ERASE` released; and a `GET` of such an array whose read raised an error where that statement never read before | `_MEM` reads the lock through the missing descriptor and the program crashes (exit code 139; `verification\v35_x66`, its comment); `GET` raises error 9, goes on with the counts of the released array and ends the program with "Out of memory" (`v35_x67`); after a read that raised an error the statement's buffer is unpacked into the array (`qb64pe.bas` 12398), and a buffer that statement never filled holds memory nobody wrote: other values on each run (`verification\v38_a`, and two recordings of `s126_owner_copies` that differed) | `_MEM` raises error 9 and gives a block that does not exist (`_MEMEXISTS` 0); `GET` raises error 9 and reads nothing; after a failed read the statement's buffer is unpacked as in the old compiler (what it read last), its bytes never read being 0 |

| D-026 | A `CONST` computed with a math function whose library is not correctly rounded (`SIN`, `COS`, `TAN`, `ATN`, `EXP`, `LOG`, `^` with a fraction, `ROOT`, `_ACOS` … `_COT`), where the values that library could give within its error bound lead to different constants | Runs its own run-time functions inside `qb64pe.exe`: the x87's `fsin`, `fcos`, `fptan`, `fpatan`, mingw's `expl` and `powl`, UCRT's `double` functions.
